podcast.body: A demo recorded by The Velvet Underground at Scepter Studios in New York on April 25, 1966. This particular version was part of a test pressing, with only two known copies ever circulated among record company executives, all of whom passed on signing the band. The band eventually signed with Verve and re-recorded their material, forgetting about these acetates. One copy was discovered by Warren Hill in a flea market box of records in New York for 75 cents in 2002, and later sold on eBay for $25,200, subsequently digitized for public access. "This is the Scepter Sessions version of Waiting for the Man."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song was part of their debut album. David Bowie became a fan of this particular track within months of the album's release, indicating its early influence. "He was a fan of a song called Scoring Smack called Waiting for the Man as early as a few months after the record came out."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
